title: New EU-Commissioned Study Highlights the Growing Nepal–Europe Migration Corridor - eeas.europa.eu
description: New EU-Commissioned Study Highlights the Growing Nepal–Europe Migration Corridor  eeas.europa.eu
publisher.title: eeas.europa.eu
full_article:
On 8 July 2025, the Nepal Economic Forum (NEF), with the support of the European Union, hosted a NEFtalk on "Nepal–Europe Migration Corridor" in Kathmandu, bringing together policymakers, migration experts, development practitioners, researchers, and diplomats to discuss one of Nepal's fastest-growing migration trends. The event also marked the presentation of findings from an EU-commissioned study examining the Nepal–Europe migration corridor, providing new evidence on migration trends, labour market dynamics, remittances, and reintegration. The discussion highlighted the importance of strengthening governance and cooperation to ensure that migration remains safe, regular, and beneficial for migrants, Nepal, and Europe alike.

The study reveals that the Nepal–Europe migration corridor has expanded significantly over the past decade, with labour permits for Europe increasing from just 4,585 in FY 2016/17 to more than 77,000 in FY 2024/25. Today, an estimated 450,000–500,000 Nepali nationals live across Europe, reflecting the growing importance of Europe as a destination for Nepali workers. While remittances continue to make a significant contribution to household incomes and Nepal's economy, the research also points to persistent challenges, including high migration costs, limited recognition of skills, fragmented governance, and continued reliance on informal recruitment intermediaries. Addressing these challenges will require stronger partnerships, improved skills matching, greater transparency in recruitment, and more effective bilateral cooperation.

Drawing on fieldwork conducted across eight European countries, the study explores the factors driving Nepali migration to Europe, including better employment opportunities, higher wages, stronger social protection systems, and increasing aspirations for education and long-term settlement. At the same time, the research highlights Europe's changing demographic landscape, where labour shortages across sectors such as healthcare, logistics, hospitality, and construction are creating growing demand for international workers. The findings underline the need for policies that better align workers' skills with labour market needs while ensuring migrants are protected throughout the migration cycle.

The study also places significant emphasis on reintegration, noting that many Nepali migrants return home with valuable skills, professional experience, savings, and entrepreneurial ambitions. Strengthening reintegration frameworks can help ensure that returning migrants are able to invest their knowledge and resources in Nepal's development, transforming migration into a catalyst for innovation, economic growth, and job creation.

A highlight of the event was the conversation between H.E. Veronique Lorenzo, Ambassador of the European Union to Nepal, and NEF Chair Sujeev Shakya, which explored Europe's evolving perspective on Nepali labour migration.

Reflecting on one of the study's notable findings, Ambassador Lorenzo observed, "One thing that stood out to me is how many women are migrating to Europe, and I don't think that's a coincidence. Europe offers a more secure path for women, and that security is bound to be a real factor drawing them to make that move."

The discussion also highlighted the importance of addressing skills mismatches, strengthening bilateral labour agreements, and supporting returning migrants so that migration can deliver long-term benefits for individuals and societies.

The research makes clear that the rapid growth of the Nepal–Europe migration corridor presents a valuable opportunity for both Nepal and the European Union. Realising this potential will depend on strengthening migration governance, improving skills recognition, reducing migration costs, expanding safe and legal pathways, and building effective reintegration systems. By promoting evidence-based policymaking and closer cooperation between governments, research institutions, and development partners, the Nepal–Europe migration corridor can continue to evolve as a model of safe, orderly, and mutually beneficial labour mobility.

The European Union remains committed to supporting initiatives that foster informed dialogue, evidence-based policymaking, and stronger international partnerships on migration. The NEFtalk and the findings of this study contribute to a growing body of knowledge that can help shape policies ensuring migration creates lasting opportunities for migrants, their families, Nepal, and Europe, reinforcing a shared vision of inclusive and sustainable development.

८ जुलाई २०२५ क नेपाल आर्थिक मंच (एनईएफ) न॑ यूरोपीय संघ केरऽ सहयोग स॑ काठमांडू म॑ "नेपाल–यूरोप माइग्रेशन कॉरिडोर" प॑ एनईएफटॉक के आयोजन करलकै, जेकरा म॑ नीति निर्माता, प्रवास विशेषज्ञ, विकास व्यवसायी, शोधकर्ता, आरू राजनयिकऽ क॑ एक साथ लानलऽ गेलै आरू नेपाल केरऽ सबसें तेजी स॑ बढ़त॑ जाय रहलऽ प्रवासन प्रवृत्ति म॑ स॑ एक के बारे म॑ चर्चा करलऽ गेलै । ई आयोजन म॑ नेपाल-यूरोप प्रवासन गलियारा के जांच करै वाला यूरोपीय संघ द्वारा कमीशन करलऽ गेलऽ अध्ययन के निष्कर्ष के प्रस्तुति भी करलऽ गेलै, जेकरा म॑ प्रवास के प्रवृत्ति, श्रम बाजार के गतिशीलता, प्रेषण, आरू पुनर्वास के बारे म॑ नया सबूत उपलब्ध कराय देलऽ गेलै । चर्चा में प्रवासी, नेपाल, आरू यूरोप के लेलऽ प्रवासन सुरक्षित, नियमित, आरू लाभकारी बनलऽ रहै लेली शासन आरू सहयोग क॑ मजबूत करै के महत्व प॑ प्रकाश डाललऽ गेलै ।

अध्ययन स॑ पता चलै छै कि पिछला एक दशक म॑ नेपाल-यूरोप प्रवासन गलियारा म॑ काफी विस्तार होय गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ यूरोप लेली श्रम परमिट वित्तीय वर्ष २०१६/१७ म॑ महज ४,५८५ स॑ बढ़ी क॑ वित्तीय वर्ष २०२४/२५ म॑ ७७,००० स॑ भी अधिक होय गेलऽ छै । आइ अनुमानित ४५०,०००–५००,००० नेपाली नागरिक सम्पूर्ण यूरोप मे रहैत अछि, जे नेपाली मजदूरक गंतव्यक रूप मे यूरोपक बढ़ैत महत्व केँ दर्शाबैत अछि । रेमिटैंस केरऽ घरेलू आय आरू नेपाल केरऽ अर्थव्यवस्था म॑ महत्वपूर्ण योगदान जारी छै, लेकिन ई शोध लगातार चुनौती के तरफ भी इशारा करै छै, जेकरा म॑ उच्च प्रवासन लागत, कौशल केरऽ सीमित मान्यता, खंडित शासन, आरू अनौपचारिक भर्ती मध्यस्थऽ प॑ लगातार निर्भरता शामिल छै । इ चुनौतियक कें सामना करय कें लेल मजबूत साझेदारी, बेहतर कौशल मिलान, भर्ती मे बेसि पारदर्शिता, आ बेसि प्रभावी द्विपक्षीय सहयोग कें आवश्यकता होयत.

आठ यूरोपीय देशऽ म॑ करलऽ गेलऽ फील्डवर्क के आधार प॑ ई अध्ययन म॑ यूरोप म॑ नेपाली प्रवासन क॑ बढ़ावा दै वाला कारकऽ के खोज करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ बेहतर रोजगार के अवसर, अधिक मजदूरी, मजबूत सामाजिक सुरक्षा प्रणाली, आरू शिक्षा आरू दीर्घकालिक बस्ती के बढ़तऽ आकांक्षा शामिल छै । एकरऽ साथ ही ई शोध यूरोप केरऽ बदलतऽ जनसांख्यिकीय परिदृश्य प॑ प्रकाश डालै छै, जहां स्वास्थ्य देखभाल, रसद, आतिथ्य, आरू निर्माण जैसनऽ क्षेत्रऽ म॑ मजदूरऽ के कमी के कारण अंतरराष्ट्रीय मजदूरऽ के बढ़तऽ मांग पैदा होय रहलऽ छै । निष्कर्ष ऐहन नीतियक कें आवश्यकता कें रेखांकित करयत छै जे श्रमिकक कें कौशल कें श्रम बाजार कें जरूरतक कें साथ बेहतर ढंग सं संरेखित करय आ इ सुनिश्चित करय छै की प्रवासी कें पूरा प्रवास चक्र मे सुरक्षा कैल जै.

अध्ययन म॑ पुनर्वास प॑ भी काफी जोर देलऽ गेलऽ छै, ई बात प॑ ध्यान देलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बहुत सारा नेपाली प्रवासी बहुमूल्य कौशल, पेशेवर अनुभव, बचत, आरू उद्यमिता के महत्वाकांक्षा के साथ घर वापस आबै छै । पुनर्समायोजन कें ढाँचा कें मजबूत करनाय इ सुनिश्चित करय मे मदद कयर सकय छै की लौटय वाला प्रवासी अपन ज्ञान आ संसाधनक कें नेपाल कें विकास मे निवेश करय मे सक्षम छै, जे प्रवास कें नवीनता, आर्थिक विकास, आ रोजगार सृजन कें उत्प्रेरक मे बदल सकय छै.

एहि आयोजनक एकटा खास बात छल एच.ई. नेपालमे यूरोपीय संघक राजदूत वेरोनिक लोरेंजो आ एनईएफक अध्यक्ष सुजीव शाक्य, जे नेपाली श्रमिक पलायन पर यूरोपक विकसित परिप्रेक्ष्यक खोज केलनि ।

अध्ययन केरऽ एगो उल्लेखनीय निष्कर्ष प॑ चिंतन करतें हुअ॑ राजदूत लोरेंजो न॑ देखलकै, "हमरा लेली एगो बात अलग छेलै कि कतेक महिला यूरोप म॑ पलायन करी रहलऽ छै, आरू हमरा नै लगै छै कि ई कोनो संजोग छै । यूरोप महिला सिनी लेली एगो अधिक सुरक्षित रास्ता पेश करै छै, आरू ई सुरक्षा एगो वास्तविक कारक होना तय छै जे ओकरा वू कदम उठाबै लेली आकर्षित करै छै ।"

चर्चा म॑ कौशल बेमेल क॑ दूर करै, द्विपक्षीय श्रम समझौता क॑ मजबूत करै, आरू वापस आबै वाला प्रवासी सिनी क॑ सहायता दै के महत्व प॑ भी प्रकाश डाललऽ गेलै ताकि पलायन स॑ व्यक्ति आरू समाज लेली दीर्घकालिक लाभ मिल॑ सक॑ ।

शोध स॑ ई बात साफ होय गेलऽ छै कि नेपाल-यूरोप प्रवासन गलियारा केरऽ तेजी स॑ वृद्धि नेपाल आरू यूरोपीय संघ दूनू लेली एगो बहुमूल्य अवसर पेश करै छै । अइ संभावना कें साकार करनाय प्रवासन शासन कें मजबूत करनाय, कौशल कें पहचान मे सुधार, प्रवासन लागत मे कमी, सुरक्षित आ कानूनी मार्गक कें विस्तार, आ प्रभावी पुनर्समायोजन प्रणाली कें निर्माण पर निर्भर करतय. साक्ष्य आधारित नीति निर्माण आ सरकारक, शोध संस्थान, आ विकास भागीदारक कें बीच घनिष्ठ सहयोग कें बढ़ावा द क नेपाल-यूरोप प्रवास गलियारा सुरक्षित, व्यवस्थित, आ पारस्परिक रूप सं लाभकारी श्रम गतिशीलता कें मॉडल कें रूप मे विकसित जारी रह सकय छै.

यूरोपीय संघ ऐन्हऽ पहलऽ के समर्थन करै लेली प्रतिबद्ध छै जे सूचित संवाद, साक्ष्य आधारित नीति निर्माण, आरू प्रवासन प॑ मजबूत अंतर्राष्ट्रीय साझेदारी क॑ बढ़ावा दै छै । एनईएफटॉक आ अइ अध्ययन कें निष्कर्ष ज्ञान कें बढ़ैत निकाय मे योगदान करयत छै जे नीतियक कें आकार देवय मे मदद कयर सकय छै जे इ सुनिश्चित करयत छै की प्रवास प्रवासी, ओकर परिवार, नेपाल, आ यूरोप कें लेल स्थायी अवसर पैदा करयत छै, जे समावेशी आ टिकाऊ विकास कें साझा दृष्टि कें मजबूत करयत छै.

Nepal-born climber Nirmal Purja, also popularly known as “Nims Dai”, is among the 10 expedition members reported missing after an avalanche struck the Broad Peak mountain in Pakistan’s Gilgit-Baltistan region.

Mr Purja was leading the multinational expedition team.

Mr Purja first gained global recognition in 2019 when he completed the seemingly impossible feat of climbing all 14 of the world’s peaks higher than 8,000m in just over six months.

The achievement, called “ Project Possible” , shattered the previous record of nearly eight years and cemented his place in mountaineering history. His journey was later documented in the Netflix film 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible .

His record was surpassed in 2023.

Before becoming a professional mountaineer, Mr Purja served for 16 years in the British military. He joined the British Army in 2003 before going on to serve in the elite Special Boat Service, one of the UK’s special forces units. He comes from a family of Gurkhas, with both his father and brothers having served in the British Army.

His achievements have earned him widespread recognition beyond the climbing community. He was appointed an MBE by Queen Elizabeth II in 2018 in recognition of his outstanding achievements in mountaineering.

As a naturalised British citizen, he has also been honoured by local authorities in the UK for his achievements.

Eastleigh Borough Council in southern England conferred on him the Honorary Freedom of the Borough, its highest civic distinction, acknowledging both his accomplishments and his contributions to the local Nepali community.

During his Everest ascent in 2019, he captured the now-iconic image of a long queue of climbers waiting to reach the summit. The photograph sparked international debate about overcrowding and safety on the world’s highest mountain.

There has been no contact with Mr Purja’s team since the incident.

However, a report in Kantipur said that Mr Purja’s GPS tracking device continued to show signs of movement after the avalanche, according to his business partner, Mingma Gyabu Sherpa.

He said the tracker initially indicated that Mr Purja had been carried downhill by the avalanche before its location shifted again, offering a glimmer of hope about his whereabouts, the outlet said.

However, it remains unclear whether the movement reflects Mr Purja himself or only the tracking device.

In 2024, Mr Purja was accused of sexual assault and harassment by at least two women, prompting calls to ban him from Mount Everest. Former Miss Finland Lotta Hintsa and April Leonardo from California accused Mr Purja of sexual misconduct during their expeditions with him. The allegations reported by the New York Times shook the mountaineering community.

At the time, his team told The Independent : “The publication’s story makes allegations, these are NOT facts. Nims denies these allegations unequivocally. We maintain the ‘investigation’ by the publication was biased and had a pre-determined narrative and outcome.”

The 10-member expedition to Broad Peak comprised six Nepali climbers – Mr Purja, Pur Bahadur Gurung (also known as Yukta), Kili Pemba Sherpa (also known as Kilu), Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa – along with Omani climber Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Chinese climber Wang Zhong, and American climber Mallory Geis, The Himalayan Times reported.

Days before the expedition, Pakistan-based adventure company Moving Mountains said the team had set off for Askole, the gateway to the Karakoram climbing season, before beginning their ascent of Broad Peak.

The company noted that the expedition marked Ms Geis’s first attempt at an 8,000-metre mountain in Pakistan, while it was expected to be Mr Sakhi’s final climb of a peak above that altitude.

Gilgit-Baltistan police say that preliminary reports indicate that four bodies have been recovered from Broad Peak following the avalanche, although the victims have not yet been identified, according to the BBC.

Authorities said efforts to gather information about the remaining climbers are ongoing as search and rescue operations continue.

In the earlier statement, ACP said: “The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range around midday today.

“President of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, Major General Irfan Arshad, HI(M), along with the senior leadership of the Club, is in constant contact with the highest government authorities and all relevant agencies to facilitate an immediate search and rescue operation.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions.

“The Alpine Club of Pakistan is closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with all concerned stakeholders.

“The Club prays for the safety and successful rescue of all the climbers and stands in solidarity with their families and the international mountaineering community during this difficult time.”

Lhakpa Sherpa, founder of 8K Expeditions and a famous climber himself, wrote on Facebook: “It is heartbreaking to wake up to the distressing news from Broad Peak.”

He called Mr Purja a “dear friend and brother” who has “elevated Nepal’s mountaineering community to the global stage”.

title: Who is Nirmal Purja, renowned Nepalese climber missing on Pakistan mountain? - The Hindu
description: Who is Nirmal Purja, renowned Nepalese climber missing on Pakistan mountain?  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal “Nimsdai” Purja and his 10-member international team are missing following a significant avalanche on Pakistan’s 8,047-metre Broad Peak. The group, last located at 6,600 metres, lost communication on Thursday (July 30, 2026), and an ongoing rescue effort involving the Pakistani Army and the Alpine Club of Pakistan is underway.

While four bodies have been recovered, the search continues for the team, which included experienced climbers from Pakistan, Oman, China and the United States.

Who is Nirmal Purja?

Born in Nepal, Purja became famous for his incredible feat of summiting all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in just over six months under his 2019 “Project Possible” expedition. The 43-year-old had climbed Annapurna, the 10th-highest mountain, on April 23, 2019, which kicked off his mission to climb all of the world’s highest peaks.

In 2021, he was part of the team of 10 Nepali climbers that made the first successful winter ascent of K2, the world’s second-highest peak.

‘14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible’ review: An extraordinary story of human endurance

Purja served in Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas and later with the Royal Marines’ Special Boat Squadron before transitioning to a career as a full-time mountaineer and guide. His accomplishments were featured in a 2021 Netflix documentary, which inspired a new generation of climbers.

He also served as an extreme cold-weather warfare specialist in the elite special forces.

What happened at Broad Peak in Pakistan?

According to information received by the Nepali Embassy in Islamabad, Purja was leading an expedition team to the 8,047-metre Broad Peak, Pakistan. The team included Pur Bahadur Gurung “Yukta”, Kili Pemba Sherpa “Kilu”, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa.

The expedition also had Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy of Oman, Sohail Sakhi of Pakistan, Wang Zhong of China and Mallory Geis of the United States.

The Broad Peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, situated in the Karakoram mountain range, was struck by an avalanche around midday Thursday. Four bodies were recovered on Friday (July 31) as search operations continue for six other climbers, including Purja.

Major General Irfan Arshad, President of the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP), announced that four bodies have been recovered. B BETA 31.07.2026. 13:54h

A curfew was imposed in several cities in southeastern Nepal today due to days of interfaith clashes that broke out on Sunday, in which at least three people were killed, authorities said.

25 people were injured in clashes between Muslims and Hindus, which broke out on Sunday evening in Diwanganju, a town in Nepal's Sunsari district on the border with India, Reuters reports.

Officials say the violence was sparked by a dispute over loud music and the display of religious flags during a Hindu gathering.

Two men were killed on Sunday in Sunsari and a third victim was reported yesterday in the neighboring Siraha district, as sporadic clashes in the area continue.

Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle said the incidents were under investigation, and no killings or clashes had been reported today.

A curfew was imposed as a preventive measure for an indefinite period in several cities to prevent a recurrence of the conflict.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah yesterday called on citizens to remain calm and for the "cloud of instability" to be removed from the country.

"The government will conduct a fair and impartial investigation into the violence and punish those responsible for the riots in a transparent manner," Shah said in a televised address to the nation.

Home Minister Sudan Gurung met with the families of those killed in Sunsari and agreed to pay each of them about $6.660 in compensation, the government said last night. He will also meet with the family of the third victim later today.

title: The Greatest Luxury Hotels On Earth Have Been Named for 2026 - Time Out Worldwide
description: The Greatest Luxury Hotels On Earth Have Been Named for 2026  Time Out Worldwide
publisher.title: Time Out Worldwide
full_article:
When you picture hotel glamour, your mind probably goes straight to Wes Anderson’s pink-hued Grand Budapest , Bill Murray looking miserable at the Park Hyatt Tokyo , or the sun-drenched clifftops of The White Lotus at Sicily’s San Domenico Palace . According to the taste-makers at Robb Report, the greatest luxury hotels are much less obvious.

The 50 Greatest Luxury Hotels on Earth 2026 list is curated by a panel of 24 luxury travel advisors who spend their lives dreaming up itineraries for the world's most demanding travellers. If you're willing to splash the cash, these luxury hotels could see you trekking to see mountain gorillas at one, or having your luggage hauled up a mountain by mule at another.

Meet the word’s five greatest hotels

Taking the top spot is Shinta Mani Mustang , a Bill Bensley-designed retreat in Nepal ’s remote Kali Gandaki River Valley, built from local Baglung stone with mountain views from every one of its 29 rooms. Guests can go horseback riding, explore ancient Buddhist monasteries, trek Mustang's high-altitude trails or try traditional Tibetan healing therapies. Not bad for a hotel that only opened in August 2023.

Photograph: Booking.com Shinta Mani Mustang

Rwanda's Singita Kwitonda takes second place. The lodge shares a physical boundary with Volcanoes National Park, so guests are living next door to a third of the world's remaining mountain gorillas. The night before your trek, staff kit you out head to toe in gaiters, boots and a poncho, hand you a packed lunch, and send you off into the mist. Come back to a heated plunge pool in every one of its eight suites.

Scotland ’s Hope Lodge rounds out the top three, proof that you don't need palm trees to make a greatest hotels list; the wild surrounds of the Scottish Highlands and a lochside setting will do just fine.

Japan’s Park Hyatt Tokyo takes the fourth spot. It occupies the top 14 floors of the Shinjuku Park Tower and includes the New York Grill and Bar on floor 52, which is the bar where Bill Murray and Scarlett Johansson’s characters get drunk together in Lost in Translation . It reopened at the end of last year after a 19 month renovation, with 26-foot floor-to-ceiling windows, Mount Fuji views on a clear day and guest rooms panelled with Hokkaido water elm wood.

Photograph: Booking.com Park Hyatt Tokyo

The rest of the top 10 spans Collegio alla Querce in Italy, London's own Claridge’s (which, incidentally, Time Out's own reviewers crowned the best hotel in London just weeks ago – Mayfair's art deco icon is clearly having a moment), Le Bristol in Paris, Panama's remote island retreat Islas Secas, and Malta’s Casa Bonavita.

The 10 greatest luxury hotels on Earth in 2026

title: Sex work or starve: Aid workers in Nepal left jobless by USAID cuts turn to sex work to survive - ap.org
description: Sex work or starve: Aid workers in Nepal left jobless by USAID cuts turn to sex work to survive  ap.org
publisher.title: ap.org
full_article:
A global investigations team of Kristen Gelineau, Bram Janssen and their translator Tulsi Rauniyar produced an exclusive, in-depth look at the impact the U.S. foreign aid cuts have had on the lives of laid-off aid workers in Nepal.

Gelineau, who has been covering the global impact of the cuts, turned a comment made to her in passing by an HIV researcher into a blockbuster package that revealed a shocking, darkly ironic fallout: Aid workers left jobless by the cuts who once provided HIV outreach to Nepal’s marginalized communities, including sex workers, have turned to sex work themselves to survive.

While much has been written about the devastating impacts the cuts have had on the people the funding once helped, far less is known about the impacts on the helpers themselves. Gelineau spent months working through layers of contacts to find and earn the trust of the aid workers, who are deeply traumatized after suffering frequent physical and sexual violence since turning to sex work. Because of Nepal’s conservative culture, these aid workers – who are themselves gender and sexual minorities – have no other options for work outside the sex industry.

Gelineau and visual journalist Janssen traveled to a small city in central Nepal, where they shadowed the women as they worked alongside a dangerous, dark highway. They were accompanied by their devoted translator Rauniyar, who worked with them until the wee hours of the morning for two weeks despite suffering from dengue fever.

The story was a massive hit with readers. It generated thousands of comments online and was shared tens of thousands of times. Gelineau heard from people who featured in the story who thanked her for shedding light on their situations, and also from readers who wanted to know how they could donate to support the laid-off aid workers.

The judges were impressed by the eye-opening investigation which was so sensitively told and the use of stunning visual techniques to tell people’s stories.

For a package that gave voice to a truly voiceless population and revealed an unknown, devastating impact of U.S. foreign policy half a world away, Gelineau, Janssen and Rauniyar win this week’s Best of AP – First Winner.

क्रिस्टन गेलिन्यू, ब्रैम जांसेन आरू हुनकऽ अनुवादक तुलसी रौनियार केरऽ एगो वैश्विक जांच टीम न॑ अमेरिकी विदेशी सहायता म॑ कटौती स॑ नेपाल म॑ छंटनी करलऽ गेलऽ सहायताकर्मी सिनी के जीवन प॑ कोन तरह के प्रभाव पड़लऽ छै, एकरऽ विशेष, गहराई स॑ नजर डाललकै ।

कटौती केरऽ वैश्विक प्रभाव क॑ कवर करै वाला गेलिन्यू न॑ एचआईवी शोधकर्ता द्वारा पास होय क॑ हुनका देलऽ गेलऽ एगो टिप्पणी क॑ ब्लॉकबस्टर पैकेज म॑ बदली देलकै जेकरा म॑ एगो चौंकाबै वाला, अन्हार विडंबनापूर्ण परिणाम के खुलासा करलऽ गेलै: एक समय म॑ सेक्स वर्कर सहित नेपाल केरऽ हाशिया प॑ पड़लऽ समुदाय क॑ एच.आई.वी.

एक तरफ जहाँ एक तरफ ई कटौती केरऽ विनाशकारी प्रभाव के बारे म॑ बहुत कुछ लिखलऽ गेलऽ छै जेकरा स॑ एक समय म॑ फंडिंग स॑ मदद मिललऽ लोगऽ प॑ पड़लऽ छै, लेकिन खुद मददगारऽ प॑ पड़ै वाला प्रभाव के बारे म॑ कहीं कम जानकारी छै । गेलिन्यू न॑ महीना भर संपर्कऽ के परतऽ के माध्यम स॑ काम करी क॑ सहायताकर्मी सिनी के विश्वास खोजै आरू अर्जित करै के काम करलकै, जे सेक्स वर्क के तरफ मुड़ला के बाद स॑ बार-बार शारीरिक आरू यौन हिंसा के शिकार होय के बाद गहराई स॑ आहत होय जाय छै । नेपाल केरऽ रूढ़िवादी संस्कृति के कारण ई सहायताकर्मी – जे खुद लैंगिक आरू यौन अल्पसंख्यक छै – के पास सेक्स उद्योग स॑ बाहर काम करै के दोसरऽ विकल्प नै छै ।

गेलिन्यू आरू दृश्य पत्रकार जानसेन मध्य नेपाल केरऽ एगो छोटऽ शहर के यात्रा करलकै, जहां वू एगो खतरनाक, अन्हार राजमार्ग के किनारे काम करतें हुअ॑ महिला सिनी प॑ छाया डाललकै । हुनका सब के साथ हुनकऽ समर्पित अनुवादक रौनियार भी छेलै, जे डेंगू के बुखार के शिकार होय के बावजूद भी दू सप्ताह तक भोर के वी घंटे तक हुनका सब के साथ काम करलकै ।

पाठकक बीच ई कथा भारी हिट भेल। एकरा ऑनलाइन हजारों कमेंट भेल आ दसों हजार बेर शेयर कएल गेल। गेलिन्यू न॑ कहानी म॑ शामिल लोगऽ स॑ सुनलकै जे हुनका धन्यवाद देलकै कि हुनी अपनऽ परिस्थिति प॑ प्रकाश डाललकै, आरू पाठकऽ स॑ भी जे ई जानना चाहै छेलै कि छंटनी करलऽ गेलऽ सहायताकर्मी सिनी के समर्थन लेली हुनी कोना दान करी सकै छै ।

जज सब आँखि खोलय बला जांच जे एतेक संवेदनशीलता स’ कहल गेल छल आ लोकक कहानी कहबा लेल आश्चर्यजनक दृश्य तकनीक के प्रयोग स’ प्रभावित छलाह.

एकटा एहन पैकेज के लेल जे सही मायने में आवाजहीन आबादी के आवाज देलक आ आधा दुनिया दूर अमेरिकी विदेश नीति के अज्ञात, विनाशकारी प्रभाव के खुलासा केलक, गेलिन्यू, जांसेन आ रौनियार एहि सप्ताह के बेस्ट ऑफ एपी – फर्स्ट विनर जीतैत छथि.
